chapters.title: A slope that changes
chapters.say: What does it mean for a curve to have a slope?

beats.say: Here is f of x equals x squared.
At x equals one, the curve is at height one, and the line that just touches it there has slope two.
Slide the point along the curve, and the slope changes with it, all the way from minus four to four.
Plot that slope at every x, and you get a straight line: two x.
And the area under that line, from zero to two, is four: the height the parabola reached.

chapters.title: Waves and circles
chapters.say: What about curves that are not y equals something?

scenes.heading: A sine wave, measured in pi

beats.say: When the x range is written in pi, the axis is marked in pi.
The sine peaks at pi over two, exactly where the cosine crosses zero.
An equation in x and y draws every point where it holds: here, a circle of radius two.
And a curve given by a parameter can be traced, like this spiral.
A curve is drawn only where its formula has a value, and never across a jump.
